Evaluate UCDP results across explicit analytical assumptions

Source: R/uncertainty.R
ucdp_sensitivity.Rd

ucdp_sensitivity() applies fatality scenarios and optional precision filters to a common data set. It can return each transformed data set or apply a user-supplied analysis function to every specification.

Usage

ucdp_sensitivity(
  data,
  scenarios = c("low", "best", "high"),
  where_prec = NULL,
  date_prec = NULL,
  fatality_missing = c("propagate", "remove", "error"),
  analysis = NULL,
  ...,
  error = c("stop", "record"),
  precision_missing = c("drop", "keep", "error")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing fatality bounds.

scenarios

Any of "low", "best", and "high".

where_prec, date_prec

Precision specifications. Supply NULL, one vector of accepted codes, or a named list of alternative code vectors.

fatality_missing

Missing-value policy applied to fatality bounds. "remove" excludes observations with incomplete triplets before the sensitivity grid is evaluated.

analysis

Optional function whose first argument receives a transformed data frame containing .ucdp_fatalities.

...

Additional arguments passed to analysis.

error

Should analysis errors stop immediately or be recorded?

precision_missing

Missing-value policy passed to ucdp_filter_precision().

Value

An object with a specification table, result table, and, when analysis = NULL, the transformed data sets.

Examples

events <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3, low = c(1, 2, 3), best = c(2, 3, 4), high = c(3, 5, 6),
  where_prec = c(1, 2, 6)
)
sensitivity <- ucdp_sensitivity(
  events,
  where_prec = list(all = NULL, precise = 1:2),
  analysis = function(x) c(total = sum(x$.ucdp_fatalities))
)
sensitivity$results
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   .specification .scenario .where_precision .date_precision total
#>            <int> <chr>     <chr>            <chr>           <dbl>
#> 1              1 low       all              all                 6
#> 2              2 low       precise          all                 3
#> 3              3 best      all              all                 9
#> 4              4 best      precise          all                 5
#> 5              5 high      all              all                14
#> 6              6 high      precise          all                 8
